display_name: ASPD-U data equipment of the PU-12M (IT-45 picture, telecode, plotting)
status: P3 of docs/PU12_DEVELOPMENT.md: the PU-12M's information chain when the player's vehicle is the post (simcore/command_post.hpp). Research: docs/research/PU12_RESEARCH_2026-10.md.
notes: Every number cited or an estimate. The telecode cycle and the plotter's time per mark are not published in what was read: the cycle is taken as one turn of the regiment's early-warning radar, the plotting time is fitted so a board of about ten targets takes a minute, SAM Simulator's cadence. The air-picture voice net (air_net_*) feeds the plotter's board from the regiment's radar battery: docs/research/PLOTTING_BOARD_2026-10.md.

max_targets.source: ru_pu12_text (information on a hundred targets, numbers 00 to 99)

semi_auto_tracks.source: ru_pu12_text (targets tracked in the semi-automatic mode: 12)

take_off_s.source: ru_pu12_text (semi-automatic take-off and sending of one target's coordinates: 2-3 s)

speed_step_mps.source: ru_pu12_text (speed in steps of 12.5 m/s, shown as a vector)

zone2_top_m.source: ru_pu12_text (H2 from 1.6 to 3.0 km; H3 from 3.2 to 25.2 km)

scales_m.notes: The P-19's own ASPD has 40, 50 and 100 km (p19_to); the PU-12M's ФР block's three positions are read as 35, 50, 100.

telecode_period_s.source: p19_to (the P-19's antenna at 6 rpm: one turn in 10 s; 12 rpm also possible); one cycle a turn of the regiment's radar is sam3d's reading

telecode_range_m.source: flak11 (PU12-1: FuG-5 R-407, the net of the regiment's automated fire control, to 15 km), valka_pu12

radar_period_s.source: p19_to (a P-19 cabled to the post: one turn at 6 rpm, 10 s)

plot_mark_s.source: estimate (one target written on the glass board: number, height, time; fitted so ten targets take about a minute, samsim_osa p20)

oriented_az_error_deg.source: estimate (an aiming-circle orientation; the later TNA-4 set's mean error is 0-20 mils, ru_pu12_text)

oriented_position_error_m.source: estimate (the position read off a 1:50 000 map)

drift_fraction.source: flak11 (PU12-0: the KP-4 course plotter's coordinates to at most 1 % of the distance travelled)

unoriented_az_error_deg.source: flak11 (PU12-0: designation errors up to 5 degrees in azimuth working with the navigation equipment)
unoriented_az_error_deg.notes: Used for a post whose GAK was never set from the aiming circle: the largest published error.

telecode_take_off_s.source: p19_to (the P-19's ASPD: the operator takes the targets' coordinates off the ASPD indicator by hand, semi-automatic take-off and sending); ru_pu12_text (one target: 2-3 s); flak11 (PU12-0: a post coupled to a radar sends its picture on by telecode); rwd_mb3 (pu12: passed on without recomputing the coordinates)
telecode_take_off_s.notes: About four targets in a 10 s cycle: with twelve each is refreshed every 30 s. The line itself is no limit: a 40-bit message at 234 baud takes 0.17 s (p19_to).

telecode_step_m.source: p19_to (the ASPD passes target coordinates in steps of 500 m on the 40 and 50 km scales, 1 000 m on the 100 km scale)
telecode_step_m.notes: The regiment's early-warning picture is taken as sent on the 100 km scale.

air_net_report_s.source: estimate (one air-situation report read out in the azimuth-range form of bguir_tsp: number, azimuth, range, identity and size, height, minute: six groups of digits)

air_net_period_s.source: bguir_tsp (a fix's time is given in minutes of the hour; heights at least every fifth report at up to two minutes between reports); narodna_armiya_2018 (the plotters' information comes every 1-2 min); samsim_osa p20 (each target's place updated every minute)
air_net_period_s.notes: Each target reported at most once a minute; with more targets than the net can read out in a minute, less often.

air_net_range_m.source: flak11 (PU12-1: FuG-1, an R-123, 15-20 km, the air-picture net, designation net no. 2, the plotters)
air_net_range_m.notes: Measured from the regiment's post, as the telecode's reach is.

air_net_az_step_deg.source: bguir_tsp (the azimuth-range report: azimuth in degrees)
air_net_az_step_deg.notes: SAM3D reads the reports in the azimuth-range form. The PVO grid's coded squares are the other form (pvo_bu_x_1984; rwd_mb3 pu12e: the board's tracks in the designation grid's squares about the radar).

air_net_range_step_m.source: bguir_tsp (the azimuth-range report: range in kilometres)

air_net_grid_levels.source: bguir_tsp (the place in the PVO grid most often to the seventh digit, the small square; less often the eighth, the additional square); rwd_mb3 (pu12e: the board's tracks plotted in the designation squares); pvo_bu_x_1984 (art. 30: positions passed by the grid's coded squares)
air_net_grid_levels.notes: The reports give the target's square (simcore/pvo_grid.hpp: big square 1 degree by 1 degree 30', its medium and small ninths) and the plotter marks its centre: a small square is about 12 by 11 km here, so a mark from the net can be some 7 km off. The tube's marks are finer. 0 would read azimuth and range instead (the steps above).
